gaps.construct: trait Captures with a required method get and a provided method as_match
gaps.description: The doc has no trait or interface declaration and no way to write an operation over 'any type that provides get'; an 'interface' block with 'given captures is a Self' is invented.

gaps.construct: default method body (as_match) inherited by every implementer, callable as self.get(0)
gaps.description: No default bodies, no Self type and no method-call form; the call on self becomes 'get 0 from captures', resolved by an unspecified dispatch rule.

No panic or unwrap; the doc has only declared failures, so the panic becomes a declared failure NoOverallMatch, which changes the signature (callers must handle or propagate it) and does not match Rust's abort-on-bug behaviour.

gaps.construct: implicit precondition that group 0 always exists for a successful match
gaps.description: The original relies on, but never states, this invariant; the honest Scribe form would be an invariant on the interface, which the doc cannot attach to a trait.

invented_syntax: an operation with a body nested inside an interface block
notes: The doc needs a distinction between 'declared failure the caller must handle' and 'bug that aborts' (Rust panic, assertion failure); without it, every unwrap or expect in Rust becomes a visible failure that ripples into every caller's header. Traits with provided methods are the core of Rust's generic style and have no counterpart at all.
